requirements.title: IAND argument restrictions
requirements.definition: I and J shall each be integer or a BOZ literal constant, matching integer kinds are required for two integer operands, and both operands shall not be BOZ literal constants.

pending.IAND-I-integer-or-boz: Use an integer I call and a BOZ-literal I call with an integer J; mutate I to real as a source-control restriction with no diagnostic facet.
pending.IAND-J-integer-or-boz: Use an integer J call and a BOZ-literal J call with an integer I; mutate J to real as a source-control restriction with no diagnostic facet.
pending.IAND-integer-kinds-match: Use same-kind integer operands selected from one declaration; mutate one operand to a distinct integer kind as a source-control restriction with no diagnostic facet.
pending.IAND-not-both-boz: Use exactly one BOZ actual argument and one integer operand; mutate both operands to BOZ literals as a source-control restriction with no diagnostic facet.

requirements.title: IAND result characteristics follow the integer operand
requirements.definition: The IAND result has the same characteristics as I for integer I, otherwise the same characteristics as J.

pending.IAND-result-kind-from-non-boz-operand: Use a nondefault integer kind for I in one call and for J in a one-BOZ call; assert KIND(result) follows the integer operand and mutate which operand is BOZ.

requirements.title: IAND converts a BOZ operand as INT to the other integer kind
requirements.definition: With either operand a BOZ literal constant, IAND first converts that operand as INT to the integer kind of the other operand.

pending.IAND-boz-converted-as-int-to-other-kind: Call IAND(Z'0F', int_value) and IAND(int_value, Z'0F') with int_value using a nondefault kind; assert selected result bits by BTEST and compare with companion calls using INT(Z'0F',kind=int_kind).

requirements.title: IAND combines bits by logical AND
requirements.definition: The IAND result bit is one exactly for operand bit pairs 1 and 1, and zero for pairs 1/0, 0/1, and 0/0, using the integer bit model of 16.3.

pending.IAND-bit-truth-table: Use operands whose bit positions cover 1/1, 1/0, 0/1, and 0/0; assert the four positions by BTEST, with an IOR intrinsic-name mutation changing the non-1/1 positions.

Classifies IAND as a elemental function; general class semantics are owned by the intrinsic framework.
Result Value paragraph is split into BOZ conversion and bit truth-table effects.
Cross-reference to the integer bit-sequence model in 16.3.

review_rationale: Source registration for 16.9.99-16.9.105: IALL, IAND, IANY, IBCLR, IBITS, IBSET and ICHAR (batch193). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer across two rounds; bit results are observed in bit context, IBITS reaches its high-bit edge, and ICHAR(CHAR(i)) == i is planned for positions the default character set is guaranteed to contain.
